Seventeen comments

Callaghans

I find this to be a lovely simple tune. I think there’s only 9 notes in it. I learnt it at a session a few years ago when I was lucky enough to spend some time in Clare. I remembered it recently when I heard “In Good Company”. They make it simple but exquisite.

↳ Posted by bd on June 3rd, 2002.

Callaghans

I seem to remember that the “Callaghan’s” on Chieftains 2 and “Paddy In The Smoke” is one of the hornpipes of that name and not this reel.

↳ Posted by Kenny on June 5th, 2002.

Cheiftans 2 and Paddy in the Smoke

That would be correct, no doubt. There’s a slight weakness with the cross-referencing of tune names on this site in that plenty of names have more than 1 tune attached to them, and all the different tunes with the name get linked. I don’t think that matters too much.

↳ Posted by bd on June 9th, 2002.

Once more, with feeling

I like this simple setting from the lads on the opening track of A Clare Conscience. Just a few choice pick up notes (including a bowed triplet in the B part) to keep the melody flowing and provide lift. This is based on Aidan McMahon’s fiddling.

X: 1
T: Callahan’s
M: 4/4
L: 1/8
S: A Clare Conscience, Aidan McMahon and Anthony Quigney
K: Dmaj

The set goes: The Galtee Ranger / Dennis Murphy’s / The Doon Reel

Great set! :-)

The Galtee Rangers, X:9

I created this version 9 to fit my own taste.

It’s 95% Copy and paste from version X:6

I remove the repeats.

I included the Part B bar 3 and 7 from version X1 : I like the sequence “fedB ABdB” better than the “fedc BcdB”, even if the “fedc BcdB” of version X:6 is more commonly used in nearly all versions here,

I fact I am pretty confident that JackB is the source of 75% of my playing and of 80% of the versions I created in The Session. Many Thanks.

↳ Posted by UPipes & harp on April 7th, 2024.
